turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I'm Sister Kavita, I'll just finish the vitals before Dr Iyer steps in. Blood pressure is one thirty-two over eighty-four, pulse seventy-eight, temperature thirty-six point six.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thanks, sister. I'm fine, really. The flyover traffic was the villain today, some procession, we just crawled.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Oxygen saturation ninety-eight percent. Weight is seventy-four kilos. Doctor will be here in a minute.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm Dr Iyer. Both of you, please sit. What brings you in?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing, doctor. I'm fine. She insisted, that's all. Too much phone at night maybe, those reels never end.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, kindly don't write fine. After he lost the job he doesn't sleep, his energy is finished, and he has no interest in anything.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Arjun, let me hear it from you. When did this start?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, when the company let me go. Three months back. No, wait, it was right after Diwali, so five months. Yes, five months.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Five months, okay. How is the night going?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I lie down and the thoughts start a race. I used to be out by eleven, now I'm awake till two, sometimes three, and I'm up again near five. Neighbour's dog also performs — yesterday he chased the paper boy, papers everywhere.
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So he manages maybe three hours, broken. In the day he sits. IPL is on and he doesn't even look, and this man lives for cricket.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Energy levels?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Low, from morning itself. Even chai feels like a project. I used to cycle to the office, and now the cycle is on the balcony with a rusted chain. I keep meaning to oil it before the whole thing seizes.
[SEG0014] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the interest is gone. Friends call, he lets it ring. Sunday lunch at his cousin's has stopped.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): In your words, have you lost interest in things you liked?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, yes. Cricket, eating out, old Hindi songs. I'm just flat. I'm fine though, I don't want you making me into a case.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nobody is making you a case. Appetite? Weight?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Appetite is less. Weight also, she says I've come down. When it started I can't say, it just happened somewhere in between.
[SEG0019] person_1 (NURSE): If it helps, doctor, last year's health-camp sheet says eighty-one kilos. That's about seven kilos down.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Noted. I have to ask this gently, the way I ask every adult who comes in low. Any thoughts of harming yourself, or of not wanting to be here?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No, doctor, I don't have those thoughts at all. My daughter is in class seven — sorry, I almost said class six, she moved up. I would never do something like that.
[SEG0022] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Same thing he tells me at home. No self-harm thoughts. He withdraws, that's the pattern.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Crying spells? Anxiety? Panic?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't cry. There is a tightness in the chest sometimes, when that HR meeting comes back to me. Not panic. If I step onto the balcony it eases.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): With that tightness, is there chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No pain, no shortness of breath, no palpitations. Just a heavy feeling, and then I remember the canteen poha. Strange, no?
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever, headache, or dizziness with all this?

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, no headache, not dizzy. I told you, it's the mood and the sleep mainly. Oh, and the society lift is broken, we climbed four floors, that's a separate suffering.

[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Climbing four floors without chest pain is actually reassuring. Let me think aloud. Five months of poor sleep, low energy, lost interest, feeling flat, after the job loss — working impression, a depressive episode, provisional, not confirmed.
[SEG0030] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His mother had depression, long back, after my father-in-law died. She took treatment for years.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you, I'll keep that in the family history. Arjun, medicines — what are you on, and what did you stop?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Sertraline. They started me at fifty milligrams... no, hundred and fifty. Ach, no, I'm mixing it up, the strip said fifty. Fifty milligrams, one tablet at night.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Still taking it?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I stopped it in March. Dull feeling, and loose motions. Maybe six weeks I took it, then I left it. Old GP wasn't informed properly, my mistake.
[SEG0035] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Zolpidem was also handed over for sleep. He never swallowed a single one. The strip is in the drawer, elaichi packets in front of it.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): So zolpidem was never taken, I won't list it as a medicine he used. Stopped sertraline, fifty milligrams at night. What about smoking and alcohol?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No smoking. A beer on weekends, not daily. Chai, three or four cups — actually five or six, I always want one more, haan.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): That much chai, especially late, will sit on the sleep. Any medicine allergy, or food allergy?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing. No allergies. Penicillin I've taken, no reaction, and food is also clear.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm going to examine you quickly. Affect looks flat, speech a bit slow, eye contact is preserved. Chest is clear, heart sounds normal, and there's no tremor.

[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Your ceiling fan is ticking, same as our Bajaj fan in Pune. Uncle used to thump it with the newspaper, and he still plays carrom with that bad knee. He says moods never leave you. I don't know about that.

[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll mention the fan to admin, and we'll come back to uncle's theory. First plan in my head was to restart sertraline today at a low dose, and to send a TSH and a full blood count today, because fatigue can be thyroid or low haemoglobin.
[SEG0043] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): TSH they already did at the company camp last month, and the SMS said normal. He is dead against tablets after those loose motions.

[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya, not today, doctor. Cousin's wedding is in Jaipur next month, and I don't want to be hunting for toilets between the sangeet and the pheras. Let me try without tablets first.

[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright, that changes what I do. I am not restarting sertraline, and I am not starting any antidepressant today. If the low mood and the sleep are still this way in four weeks, we might start mirtazapine, which is often kinder for sleep. Might — not a prescription now.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Mirtazapine, that is a new name. Will it also give loose motions? I'm just asking, not agreeing.

[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fair question. It more often causes sleepiness and a bigger appetite than loose motions. Still, I am not prescribing it today. We only consider it if you are no better when we meet again.

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Blood tests, same shift. I won't send them today, the TSH was normal last month and there is no new medicine. We might repeat a full blood count and a TSH if things have not settled in four weeks.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Then what do I actually do from tonight?

[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): No chai after four in the afternoon. Same waking time every day, bad night or not. Walk twenty minutes most days. And if any thought of harming yourself appears, you come to us or to emergency the same day, you don't sit on it.
[SEG0051] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Chai I will police. On other things he argues, on food he obeys.

[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): For review I was going to say three weeks. No, four weeks gives the routine a proper chance, so let's see you back in four weeks. If you worsen before then, come earlier, don't hold the date.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Four weeks I can do. So this is not a permanent stamp? Uncle's theory is sitting in my head now, along with his carrom scores.

[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not permanent, and not a stamp. People recover with structure, with family around them, and sometimes with medicine later. My impression stays provisional, depression after the job loss, and we look again in four weeks before any tablet.
[SEG0055] person_1 (NURSE): Book the four-week slot at reception, doctor? And any blood forms?
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, book a routine review in four weeks. No forms today.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. Sister, your cuff was ice cold, just an observation. If we don't leave now the flyover will eat the evening.
[SEG0058] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We will come. I'll keep a note of his sleep and whether he starts answering calls.
[SEG0059] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please do. Arjun, you did well to talk today, even after walking in saying you were fine.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Haan, well. Don't tell my cousin I discussed toilets and pheras in the same breath. See you in four weeks, doctor.

spec.situation: Adult with poor sleep, low energy and loss of interest for months after a job loss or bereavement; partner or parent speaks for them; patient says 'I'm fine' then partly opens up; denies thoughts of self-harm clearly (doctor asks gently); medication discussed but not started today.
features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.reason: Job loss five months ago is supported; 'not working' and reported_by patient are not explicitly stated together.
bad.text: occupation (description=Lost his company job five months ago and is not working, status=former, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: TSH was completed and family member reported it; not requested by family member.

omissions.text: Insomnia details were not recorded: previously slept by 11 pm, now awake until 2–3 am and wakes again near 5 am, with only about 3 hours of broken sleep.
Patient denied not wanting to be here / passive death wishes, in addition to denying self-harm thoughts.
Anxiety was asked about and not recorded; patient described chest tightness when reminded of the HR meeting and said it was not panic.
Allergy history was more specific than recorded: no medicine allergies and no food allergies; he has taken penicillin without any reaction.
Medication history omission: zolpidem had been prescribed for sleep but was never taken at all; doctor explicitly said not to list it as a medicine he used.
Sertraline stop date and reason were not recorded: he stopped it in March because it caused a dull feeling and loose motions, and he had not informed the old GP.

There was an explicit plan change not captured: the doctor considered restarting sertraline at a low dose initially, but after discussion decided not to restart sertraline and not to start any antidepressant today.
TSH result context is recorded incorrectly: family reported TSH was already done at the company camp last month and was normal; it was not requested/completed by the family member.
Doctor advised that no blood tests would be sent today; no forms today.
